key_insight: HCM-PhenotypeNet combines echocardiographic video and clinical data to automatically group hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients into four clinically distinct phenotypes.
clinical_relevance: These phenogroups may help refine HCM risk stratification and personalize management by highlighting differences in obstruction, genetics, age of onset, and heart-failure burden.
method: Deep neural network extracted features from 1,553 echocardiography video clips.
More than 100 clinical variables from 156 patients were fused into patient-level representations.
UMAP and Deep Embedded Clustering (DEC) were used to identify and validate phenogroups.
evidence_signal: The best model used DEC with 4 clusters and showed strong separation (silhouette ~0.89), with clinically interpretable subgroups and no mortality difference detected in this cohort.
watch_item: The phenogroups were derived from a single relatively small cohort, so external validation is needed before clinical use.
paper_title: HCM-PhenotypeNet: Deep Multimodal Phenotyping of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy from Echocardiographic Video and Clinical Data
